subject: POC trial env: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica.park@acme.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: POC trial env: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC - next steps

Hi Jessica / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time on the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps based on the discovery: 

POC objective / success criteria (as I captured):
- Latency: 95th pctile generation latency < 350ms for 512-token prompts under expected concurrent RPS (10-20 RPS).
- Throughput: sustain ~500k tokens/day for the evaluation window without throttling.
- Cost: target cost per 1k tokens under $0.70 for production-like runs.
- Functional: model outputs meet current A/B quality baseline (we'll use your 500 prompt eval set).

Evaluation plan & ownership:
- Acme: provide the evaluation prompt set, baseline metrics, and a sample data subset for tracing (Tom / Jessica).
- Redwood: spin up trial environment, run ramped load tests, collect latency/cost breakdowns, and run the evaluation harness against your prompt set (Marissa / David).

Environment options (pros/cons):
1) Hosted trial (fastest) – Redwood-managed, no network setup, quick onboarding in 1 business day. Good to validate latency/cost and functional quality.
2) Dedicated sandbox – reserved GPU pool in our infra tied to your account. Predictable throughput; good if you want production-like load and isolation. 3–5 business days to provision.
3) VPC trial (private) – customer VPC peering / private deployment for regulated data. Full isolation and KMS integration, but prep and security review required; estimate 2–3 weeks.

Recommended next step: start with a hosted trial for the first 2 weeks to validate quality and metrics, then move to a dedicated sandbox if you need production-like throughput/isolation. If compliance requires, we can run parallel security checks for a VPC trial.

Proposed timeline:
- Friday (8/6): kickoff + runbook + access details (Marissa)
- Week of 8/9: hosted trial live, dry runs and smoke tests
- Week of 8/16: load tests + evaluation harness runs; share results and cost breakdown

Attachments: redwood-poc-runbook-ACME-v1.pdf (runbook) and env-option-matrix.xlsx (comparison).

Action items:
- Jessica: confirm the evaluation prompt set and whether any prompts contain PII (so we can adjust logging).
- Tom: confirm desired start date for the hosted trial (we recommend 8/10).
- David / Michael: please review the runbook and confirm availability for the kickoff.

Thanks — happy to adjust.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
